  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Email change without password re-entry enables account takeover persistence",
      "scenario": "An attacker who briefly hijacks a session (e.g. via XSS, shared device, or stolen cookie) can silently change the account's email address with no password confirmation, letting them later use 'forgot password' on the new email to fully lock out the real owner.",
      "component": "Email change handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "The change takes effect immediately without re-entering the password."}],
      "asvs": ["V6.2.1", "V6.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-620"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone who grabs a live session can change the email with no password check, then take over the account for good.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require re-authentication before sensitive profile changes",
        "given": "A logged-in user requests to change their email, phone, or shipping address",
        "when": "The change request is submitted",
        "then": "The system must require password re-entry or step-up authentication before applying the change"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No confirmation or notification on email/contact change",
      "scenario": "Because the change takes effect immediately with no stated notification step, a victim has no way to know their email or address was changed until it's too late to react, and there's no verification that the new email actually belongs to the account owner.",
      "component": "Email change handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "The account settings page lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address. The change takes effect immediately"}],
      "asvs": ["V6.2.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-287"],
      "plainLanguage": "When your email gets changed, nobody gets told — the real owner finds out too late.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Notify and verify on contact info changes",
        "given": "A user's email, phone, or address is changed",
        "when": "The change is saved",
        "then": "The system must notify the old email/phone and require verification of the new email before it becomes active"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Long-lived 30-day session cookie extends attacker window after any hijack",
      "scenario": "Since sessions persist for 30 days in a cookie, any attacker who steals the cookie (via XSS, malware, or a shared/public computer) has a full month to perform sensitive actions like changing the email, address, or phone, far longer than a session timeout would normally allow.",
      "component": "Session cookie",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Sessions are kept in a cookie for 30 days."}],
      "asvs": ["V3.3.1", "V3.3.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "Stolen login cookies stay valid for a whole month, giving attackers a long time to misuse them.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit session lifetime and re-verify for sensitive actions",
        "given": "A session cookie is older than a short idle/absolute threshold",
        "when": "A sensitive action like changing email or address is attempted",
        "then": "The system must require re-authentication regardless of remaining cookie validity"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Shipping address change enables silent order/delivery redirection",
      "scenario": "An attacker with a hijacked session can change the shipping address immediately with no re-verification, redirecting future deliveries or account-linked physical mail (e.g. payment cards, password reset letters) to an address they control.",
      "component": "Account settings page",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "The account settings page lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address."}],
      "asvs": ["V6.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-620"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could quietly change where your packages or sensitive mail get sent.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect shipping address changes like other sensitive data",
        "given": "A user requests a shipping address change",
        "when": "The change is submitted",
        "then": "The system must require step-up verification and notify the account owner"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "PII and credential-adjacent fields exposed on a single settings page without stated access controls",
      "scenario": "The settings page holds email, phone and address (PII) and sits behind only normal session auth; if session validation is weak or the page lacks server-side authorization checks per field, an attacker could view or modify another user's PII via parameter manipulation (e.g. changing a user/account ID).",
      "component": "Account settings page",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Deterministic signals: {\"dataClasses\":[\"pii\",\"credentials\"]"}],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1", "V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the page doesn't double-check who owns the data, one user might see or edit another user's personal info.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce server-side object-level authorization on settings data",
        "given": "A request to view or modify profile fields",
        "when": "The request is processed",
        "then": "The server must verify the authenticated session owns the target account/profile before returning or applying changes"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Summary: I built a 6-threat STRIDE model for EVAL-03 (Account settings with email change), focused on the lack of re-authentication for email/phone/address changes, missing old-email notification, likely missing CSRF protection, and the 30-day session cookie extending the attack window. Top risks are the password-less email change enabling account takeover (Critical-ish, 4/5) and the missing old-email notification hiding the takeover.
